findings.title: Image fetch reads the whole body before any size check
findings.description: fetch() calls r.read() with no byte cap and only checks the magic bytes afterwards, so a large or slow https response is fully buffered.

trace.description: the URL comes from regex-extracted OCR markdown (https-only allowlisted)
data = r.read() buffers the entire response

evidence.description: data = r.read() has no max_bytes argument
the magic check runs after the body is already in memory

verification.method: source-only reading of fetch() (:94-117) plus a runtime probe with a simulated HTTPS transport (urlopen patched to a 64 MiB non-magic BytesIO; no network)
verification.observed: fetch returned: bad magic (67108864 bytes) — the full 64 MiB body was buffered before the magic-byte gate; dest written: False; peak RSS 154804 KB for a 64 MiB send (growth proportional to body size)
verification.notes: Transport simulated at urlopen; the size behaviour is transport-independent because read() takes no limit argument. A 30 s urlopen timeout and the https-only scheme gate bound throughput, not read size.

findings.root_cause: fetch() reads the http response with r.read() and NO byte argument before the magic-byte test — the entire response body is buffered in memory, and the module consults no Content-Length and no read ceiling anywhere (its only size logic was the local-file gate at :83, which checks fetched NOTHING).
findings.intended_behavior: the response read is bounded to a fixed ceiling; a body larger than the ceiling is never fully buffered (read(), the http read, is capped at MAX_IMAGE_BYTES plus one probe byte), is reported skipped, and is never written to disk.

conditions.description: image URLs point at an external https CDN (ufileos) whose response sizes the repo does not control; URLs are regex-extracted from OCR markdown.
fetches run concurrently (ThreadPoolExecutor, --workers default 8), so several oversized buffers could grow at once.

execution.attacker_perspective: a newsletter markdown row pointing at a large https resource (or an attacker-influenced one, since URLs are regex-extracted from OCR markdown) makes the capture read the whole body into memory before any validation; --workers N rows run concurrently and amplify it.
execution.observed_result: with a simulated https transport (urlopen patched to a 64 MiB non-magic BytesIO; no network): 'fetch returned: bad magic (67108864 bytes)' — the full 64 MiB body was buffered BEFORE the magic-byte gate; dest written: False; /usr/bin/time -v peak RSS 154804 KB for the 64 MiB send (growth proportional to body size). Pre-remediation.
payloads: a non-magic 64 MiB https response body (no JPEG/PNG header)
instructions: at ref 8e338436 (pre-remediation) read helpers/pdf/capture_newsletter_images.py:94-117 — r.read() has no byte argument
run the probe: PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python3 /mnt/data/tmp/opencode/verify_unbounded_read.py (urlopen patched; transport simulated; no network)

remediation.strategy: cap the http read at a fixed ceiling: r.read(MAX_IMAGE_BYTES + 1) — at most one probe byte past the ceiling; a larger body is reported skipped and never buffered further or written. The 30 s urlopen timeout and the https-only scheme gate (SEC-6) already bound throughput; the ceiling bounds memory.

code_changes.description: MAX_IMAGE_BYTES (64 MiB) read ceiling in fetch(); oversized bodies return 'skipped oversized body (> N bytes)' and are never written
regression: oversized body skipped + never written; exactly-at-ceiling magic body still writes; ceiling does not downgrade small bodies

remediation.status: applied 2026-10-20 — tree left dirty for the operator (house rule: no agent commits)

likelihood.reason: requires an oversized https resource linked from a newsletter's OCR markdown; the channel is the newsletter CDN convention and the exposure is incidental, not attacker-targeted.

impact.reason: demonstrated: memory consumption grows with the attacker-chosen body size (64 MiB fully buffered; peak RSS 154804 KB, growth proportional); a sufficiently large body exhausts capture-worker memory and kills the run — full OOM not demonstrated in the probe.

severity.overall_severity_reason: bounded below the demonstrated impact (R1): the mechanism is confirmed end-to-end, but the channel is indirect and the probe demonstrated proportional buffered growth, not a crash.

confidence.reason: runtime probe observed the buffered byte count directly (67108864 bytes returned by read()); the size behaviour is transport-independent because read() accepts a limit argument by contract.
